names.pk_Server: The server's public key, carried in the end-entity certificate of its Certificate message and used to verify its CertificateVerify signature (§4.4.2, §4.4.3).
names.sk_Server: The server's private signing key, matching the public key in its end-entity certificate, with which it signs CertificateVerify (§4.4.2, §4.4.3).
names.PSK: The pre-shared key in use, either established externally or derived from the resumption_master_secret of a previous connection, input to HKDF-Extract to form the Early Secret (zero if no PSK is used) (§2.2, §4.6.1, §7.1).
names.server_certificates: The identity scope of the server identities clients authenticate through certificates chaining to their trust anchors; open means the attacker may obtain a valid certificate for a server identity of its own (§4.4.2, §4.4.2.2).
names.psk_identities: The identity scope of the PSKs clients and servers share, external or established through NewSessionTicket, which a client names by a PskIdentity in its pre_shared_key extension and a server accepts after validating the binder; open means the attacker shares PSKs of its own with honest endpoints (§2.2, §4.2.11).
names.dh_group: The (EC)DHE group of the key exchange, one of the named groups of the client's supported_groups for which it sends a key_share, answered by the server's key_share in its ServerHello (§4.2.7, §4.2.8).
names.hash_algorithm: The cipher suite hash algorithm, used by Transcript-Hash and HKDF and so for the transcript hash the server signs in CertificateVerify (§7.1, §4.4.1, §4.4.3, §B.4).
names.aead_algorithm: The AEAD algorithm of the negotiated cipher suite, which protects the records; for 0-RTT data, that of the cipher suite associated with the PSK (§5.2, §4.2.10, §B.4).
names.Client: The client, the endpoint initiating the TLS connection (§1.1).
names.Server: The server, the endpoint which did not initiate the TLS connection (§1.1).
names.random_Client: ClientHello.random, the client's 32 bytes from a secure random number generator (§4.1.2).
names.random_Server: ServerHello.random, the server's 32 bytes from a secure random number generator (§4.1.3).
names.offer_Client: The client's offer in its ClientHello for the parameters the server will select: the protocol versions, the cipher suites (AEAD algorithm and hash), the key-exchange groups with key_share, and the PSK and its psk_key_exchange_modes (§4.1.1, §4.1.2).
names.selected_parameters_Server: The parameters the server selects from the offer in its ServerHello: the version, the cipher_suite (AEAD algorithm and hash), the key-exchange group of its key_share, and whether and which PSK is used (§4.1.1, §4.1.3).
names.application_write_key_Client: The client application traffic key, client_write_key derived with HKDF-Expand-Label from client_application_traffic_secret_0 (§7.1, §7.3).
names.application_write_key_Server: The server application traffic key, server_write_key derived with HKDF-Expand-Label from server_application_traffic_secret_0 (§7.1, §7.3).
names.exporter_master_secret: exporter_master_secret, Derive-Secret(Master Secret, "exp master", ClientHello...server Finished), the secret behind keying material exporters (§7.1, §7.5).
names.per_record_nonce: The per-record nonce of the AEAD-protected record carrying the data, the padded 64-bit sequence number XORed with the sender's write_iv (§5.3).
names.additional_data: The AEAD additional data input of a protected record, the record header TLSCiphertext.opaque_type || TLSCiphertext.legacy_record_version || TLSCiphertext.length (§5.2).
names.application_data_Client: The client's 1-RTT application data (TLSInnerPlaintext.content of a record of type application_data), sent after its Finished under keys derived from client_application_traffic_secret_N (§2, §5.2, §7.3).
names.application_data_Server: The server's application data (TLSInnerPlaintext.content of a record of type application_data), sent under keys derived from server_application_traffic_secret_N (§2, §5.2, §7.3).
names.early_data_Client: The client's 0-RTT early data, application data sent in its first flight under keys from client_early_traffic_secret, whose security properties the document calls weaker than those of other TLS data (§2.3, §4.2.10, §7.3).

properties.description: In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the client completes a 1-RTT handshake, a distinct server run reached its Finished with the same randoms, PSK, server public key, offered and selected parameters, application traffic keys and exporter_master_secret.

In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the client completes a 1-RTT handshake, a server reached its Finished with the same randoms, PSK, server public key, offered and selected parameters, application traffic keys and exporter_master_secret.

In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), the attacker never learns the client application traffic key of a handshake the client completed.

In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), the attacker never learns the client's 1-RTT application data.

In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), the attacker never learns the client's 0-RTT early data.

In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the client accepts a 1-RTT record, the server sent that data in a session with the same randoms, PSK and server public key, under the same per-record nonce and additional data (replay is left to the receiver refusing a repeated nonce).

In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the server accepts a client 1-RTT record, the client sent that data in a session with the same randoms, PSK and server public key, under the same per-record nonce and additional data (replay is left to the receiver refusing a repeated nonce).

In the reftls model of RFC 8446, where every handshake uses a PSK with (EC)DHE and the server also authenticates with its certificate (a combination the RFC does not specify, §2.2, §E.1), when the server accepts 0-RTT early data, the client sent it in a session with the same ClientHello.random and PSK, under the same per-record nonce and additional data (non-injective: 0-RTT data can be replayed).

The library's sanity check that, when a client completes a TLS 1.2 handshake, a server completed one with the same parameters; this TLS 1.3-only model runs no TLS 1.2 process, so the query holds vacuously.
properties.gap: sanity: a sanity query of the shared TLS library about TLS 1.2 handshake events, which this TLS 1.3-only model never raises; it holds vacuously and states no goal of RFC 8446

properties.description: Reachability check: a server completes a TLS 1.2 handshake (ServerFinished); this TLS 1.3-only model runs no TLS 1.2 process, so the event is unreachable (true).
properties.gap: sanity: a reachability check of a protocol event (false means the event is reachable), not a security goal

properties.description: Reachability check: a client completes a TLS 1.2 handshake (ClientFinished); this TLS 1.3-only model runs no TLS 1.2 process, so the event is unreachable (true).
properties.gap: sanity: a reachability check of a protocol event (false means the event is reachable), not a security goal

properties.description: Reachability check: a server can complete a TLS 1.3 handshake (ServerFinished, after the client's Finished); false means the event is reachable.
properties.gap: sanity: a reachability check of a protocol event (false means the event is reachable), not a security goal

properties.description: Reachability check: a server can reach its TLS 1.3 Finished (PreServerFinished); false means the event is reachable.
properties.gap: sanity: a reachability check of a protocol event (false means the event is reachable), not a security goal

properties.description: Reachability check: a client can complete a TLS 1.3 handshake (ClientFinished); false means the event is reachable.
properties.gap: sanity: a reachability check of a protocol event (false means the event is reachable), not a security goal

properties.description: Unique channel binding: no client session and server session that differ in ClientHello.random, ServerHello.random or the server's public key share the channel binding the model records, the exporter_master_secret (§7.5); true.
properties.gap: missing subtype: uniqueness of the channel binding (the exporter_master_secret) across sessions, a key-uniqueness goal

properties.description: Unique resumption secret: no client session and server session that differ in ClientHello.random, ServerHello.random or the server's public key end with the same resumption_master_secret (§7.1); true, where the model's comment expects TLS 1.2 to fail.
properties.gap: missing subtype: uniqueness of the resumption_master_secret across sessions, a key-uniqueness goal

properties.description: Unique ticket PSK: no client session and server session that differ in ClientHello.random, ServerHello.random or the server's public key derive the same resumption PSK, HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption_master_secret, "resumption", ticket_nonce, Hash.length) (§4.6.1); true.
properties.gap: missing subtype: uniqueness of the per-ticket resumption PSK across sessions, a key-uniqueness goal

properties.description: Reachability check: a client or server can derive a resumption PSK from a NewSessionTicket's ticket_nonce after the handshake, PSK = HKDF-Expand-Label(resumption_master_secret, "resumption", ticket_nonce, Hash.length) (§4.6.1); false means the event is reachable.
properties.gap: sanity: a reachability check of a protocol event (false means the event is reachable), not a security goal

properties.description: Unique traffic keys: no client session and server session that differ in ClientHello.random, ServerHello.random or the server's public key end with the same client and server application traffic keys (§7.3); true.
properties.gap: missing subtype: uniqueness of the application traffic keys across sessions, a key-uniqueness goal
